external_sources.scope: Primary author exposition; original typeset statement and hypotheses inspected, including r >= n >= 2 and selected-place independent algebraic forms. Used in the algebraic alternative and fixed-term unit-sum argument; not locally formalized.

external_sources.name: Schlickewei, The p-adic Thue-Siegel-Roth-Schmidt theorem, Archiv der Mathematik 29 (1977), 267-270
external_sources.scope: Original theorem attribution and bibliography. Publisher DOI could not be opened here; the precise formulation was checked in the Evertse primary-author exposition.

external_sources.name: Corvaja and Zannier, A subspace theorem approach to integral points on curves
external_sources.scope: Theorem 1 and S-integral extension inspected. Siegel input to the prior fixed-source curve-avoidance theorem; not locally formalized.

external_sources.name: Weaver and fourier_wren, paper 48 v2
external_sources.scope: Named analytic input F. Lemma 7, equation (76), and bounded-branch proof of Theorem 8 inspected, retaining central totals, fixed ordinary targets, bounded real offset and linear extra ternary precision. No claim of complete independent verification of the analytic paper.

external_sources.name: Shaik, polylogarithmic Collatz trajectory paper v4.0.2 (2026-10-04)
external_sources.scope: Named analytic input H. Corollary 1.2 and the actual shortcut odd-count estimate in the time-control proof of Proposition 6.4 inspected. Endpoint equality alone is insufficient. External formalization archive was not rebuilt.

external_sources.name: Inselmann, An Approximation of the Collatz Map and a Lower Bound for its Average Total Stopping Time, arXiv:2402.03276v3
external_sources.scope: Theorem 2.18 full-trajectory statement at the maximal horizon with power-density exceptions inspected. Source-qualified alternative to H for the weaker o(e) conclusion; not formalized.

external_sources.name: Krasikov and Lagarias, Bounds for the 3x+1 problem using difference inequalities, arXiv:math/0205002
external_sources.scope: Primary paper abstract and exponent .84 inspected. The manuscript uses the frozen PR197/PR200 predecessor-based rigidity interface; no new proof of that counting theorem is claimed.

external_sources.name: Lagarias, The Ultimate Challenge: The 3x+1 Problem, overview
external_sources.scope: Classical ordinary all-odd trajectory formula is attributed for context and independently rederived in the new finite arithmetic.
